answer: A work-weighted reputation makes fake identities expensive: every agent must earn attestations by doing verifiable work over time, like a cedar growing slowly, so a flood of fresh accounts has no standing. Attackers face a ripple effect — each new identity starts at zero and pays the same time cost again, while an oasis of trusted, long-lived agents anchors the economy. A thousand Sybils cost a thousand slow histories, not one cheap script.
